newsitem.title: USA: Choice Hotels says to split into two cos.
newsitem.headline: Choice Hotels says to split into two cos.

text.p: Choice Hotels International Inc said Tuesday it planned by fall 1997 to split into two entities, a hotel franchising company and a real estate company with owned and managed hotel properties.
The company said the deal would be structured as a pro-rata, tax-free spinoff to shareholders, conditional on an affirmative ruling from the Internal Revenue Service.

It said Choice's franchising operations, comprised of Clarion, Quality, Comfort, Sleep, Rodeway, Econo Lodge and MainStay brands, will be distributed to Choice's shareholders and will be named Choice Hotels International Inc.
A separately managed real estate company will own and manage 70 hotels in the United States, with 20 hotels currently under construction or in development, the company said in a prepared statement.
It said the spinoff will involve a special dividend to shareholders who will own an interest in each of the two companies, with the deal also contingent on ratification by Choice shareholders.

Stewart Bainum Jr., chairman of the board, will be chairman of the boards of each of the entities, the statement said, adding that the Bainum family would have about a 32 percent ownership interest in both companies..

"The division into two different companies will enable us to achieve our strategy of separating the owned and managed hotel properties from the pure franchising business, thus allowing each entity to leverage its respective core strengths," Baimum said.

"In addition to allowing greater strategic focus, the spin-off will eliminate any perceived conflicts by franchisees with regard to preferential treatment of the company's owned hotels," said William R. Floyd, vice chairman and chief executive officer.
Floyd will be vice chairman and chief executive officer of Choice Hotels International Inc, the statement said, with no decisions yet made regarding senior management for the real estate company.
